Q116272858.summary: The Virgin, veiled and haloed, sits on a cushioned throne between columns, holding the Christ Child upright on her lap; the Child, with his own halo, raises his hand. Two winged angels lean over the canopy above, and a border of acanthus frames the scene. The plaque presents Christ as the incarnate Lord seated in his mother's lap, the throne of the Divine Wisdom.
facts: The Met dates the plaque to 850–875 and attributes it to northern France (accession 17.190.39, gift of J. Pierpont Morgan, 1917).
Its size (14.5 × 8.8 cm) and design match The Met's companion plaque of Christ enthroned with two apostles (17.190.41).
Q116272858.notes: Whether the two Met plaques were originally part of the same object was not verified.
